sentences.text:
Kanha vs National Insurance Company Ltd. on 8 October, 2025
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 8 th Of October, 2025

Misc. Appeal No. 3480 of 2018
 Kanha And Others
 Versus
 National Insurance Company Ltd.

And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Sameer Verma, learned counsel for the petition  Shri Manoj Kumar Soni, learned counsel for the resp  ORDER
The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 23.03.2018 passed in MACC No.8113010/2016 challenging the quantum of compensation.

2. The facts of the case are that on 24.11.2015 at around 04 p.m. the deceased Pooja was going with her husband and daughter by the side of the road towards her village-Sannod, when they reached village Bagadadaa a motorcycle bearing registration number MP41-MD-9623 came which was being ridden by its rider in rash and negligent manner and dashed into Pooja from behind because of which she sustained grievous injuries.
She was rushed to Sanskar hospital, Dewas where she was declared brought dead.
3. The appellants/claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Pooja.

The claims tribunal after recording the evidence concluded on the assessment of 2 MA-3480-2018 the same that the appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,82,000/- out of which amount of Rs.6,12,000/- was for loss of dependency.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal has incorrectly taken the income of the deceased at Rs.3000/- per month on notional basis whereas the deceased was earning Rs.9000/- per month by doing stitching work.
He further submits that nothing has been added for future prospects.

Although looking to the age of the deceased as 26 years on the date of the accident,
40% addition should have been made in her income.
He also points out that even in other heads meager amount has been awarded and for amount of consortium only an amount of Rs.40,000/-
has been awarded whereas the claimants are father and daughter of the deceased and both are entitled for compensation for loss of consortium.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company points out that while assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.3000/- per month, the entire amount has been taken into consideration for Kanha vs National Insurance Company Ltd. on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152624925/
1 assessing compensation without making deduction for personal expenses.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the shortcoming in the income has been compensated by not deducting any amount for personal expenses.
Hence, no interference is warranted with the impugned award, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

On perusal of the record and the findings recorded in para 14, this Court is of the considered view that the claim of earning of Rs.9000/- per month has rightly been rejected by the claims tribunal because there is no 3 MA-3480-2018 material at all to believe the same.
However, the income of the deceased Pooja has been taken on notional basis at Rs.3000/- per month without there being any reference of relevant factors for the same.
It is trite law that contribution of a house-maker is also not any lessor than the contribution of any earning member of the family.

Hence, her contribution should be taken at least at the minimum wages prescribed for unskilled labourer at the relevant time which as per the guidelines of the State Legal Services Authority was Rs.6575/- per month which is taken as the income of the deceased.

8. Considering the age of the deceased as 26 years, 40% addition is made under the head of future prospects in income of the deceased in terms of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16) SCC 680 .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Looking to the number of dependents, the deduction in the head of personal expenses is made at 1/3rd.

As such, the amount for compensation for loss of dependency would now come to Rs.12,05,880/-.
9.

In view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case o f Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1249, both the appellants-claimants are entitled for spousal/parental consortium being husband and daughter of the deceased.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1249
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, both of them are awarded Rs.44000/- each which is totaling to Rs.88000/-.

The amount of loss of estate and funeral expenses is hereby modified to Rs.16,500/- each as such the total compensation would now come to Rs.13,72,880/- and after deducting the already amount of 4 MA-3480-2018 Rs.6,82,000/-, the appellants are now entitled for payment of Rs.6,90,880/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
10. It is seen from the record that the appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.3 Lacs, thus, they are to pay deficit court fees within a period of four weeks from today.
If the court fees is not paid within this period then interest shall not apply on the enhanced amount of compensation beyond the period of 4 weeks.
11. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
